sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:34474
Court No. - 65

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 6133 of 2025
Applicant :- Anurag Gupta

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Bilas Prasad
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard SriRam Bilas Prasad, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Jai Kishan Chaurasiya, learned State Law Officer as well as perused the material placed on record.
3.
As informant by learned State Law Officer, notice to the informant has been served on 19.02.2025, but none is present on behalf of the informant even in the revised list.

4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 27 of 2024, under Sections 376, 507 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 67 of I.T. Act, Police Station Jangipur, District Ghazipur, during the pendency of trial.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
It is next Anurag Gupta vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137307022/

entities.text: Anurag Gupta vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 stated that the victim has been examined as PW-1 during trial and she has completely resiled from her earlier statement and has been cross-examined by the public prosecutor after declaring her hostile.
There is no likelihood of conviction of the applicant in the present case.
Learned counsel has further stated that there is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 22.03.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant- Anurag Gupta, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
9. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

10. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 10.3.2025 Sumit S (Justice Krishan Pahal)
